title: Architecture work
description: The files the architecture team of one Epic hands to each other and to the script: the solutions architect's state and result, the requests it writes for the agents it starts and their answers, a reviewer's result for the unapproved content, the lead's routing, the question put to the decider and its ruling, and the comparison of what a Story built. The root is the architect's result; each other file has its own schema file that refers to its definition here. A matrix id is the id of a row as atw-matrix prints it. The review scope a reviewer is handed is defined by matrix.schema.json ($defs/ReviewScope).

NeedState.description: `approved`: the architecture for the need exists and the matrix marks it approved. `disagreement`: it exists and is approved, and two statements disagree. `missing`: no approved statement meets the need.

StateConclusion.description: `complete-and-approved`: every need is `approved`. `work-remains`: at least one need is `disagreement` or `missing`.

Conclusion.description: `complete-and-approved`: everything the PRD needs existed and was approved, and no arc42 document changed. `ready-for-review`: the architect designed or settled something and it is ready for review. `unsettled`: at least one matter is listed in `unsettled`.

CriterionStatus.description: `satisfied`: `satisfiedAt` names where. `not-applicable`: `reason` says why the criterion does not apply to this PRD.

UnsettledKind.description: `technical-choice`: two positions remain, each with evidence and a real cost. `business-conflict`: two business requirements that no design meets together, or a design that only works against section 2.

RequestKind.description: `question`: one question to answer. `task`: one bounded piece of design, or one diagram to draw.

TrdMode.description: `draft`: write the TRD from the PRD and the approved arc42 material. `update`: apply the listed changes and nothing else.

RequirementKind.description: `obligation`: something that must be true of an element, with a checkable value. `reuse`: the element obtains a behaviour from a shared capability and does not implement its own.

Routing.description: What the lead decides for one item. `reject`: the finding goes no further. `correct`: the architect corrects it and the reviewer that raised it re-checks. `opinion`: one specialist is asked, and the answer goes to the architect with the correction. `competing-design`: the architect designs the other position of one matter. `decider`: the decider rules.

OwnerConcernKind.description: `business-conflict`: two business requirements cannot both be met by any design. `section-2-conflict`: the only workable design conflicts with a section 2 constraint.

Citation.description: Where something is stated or can be checked.

source.description: An arc42 path relative to the architecture root, a PRD or TRD path, an AWS documentation URL, or code as repository, revision and file:line.

heading.description: The heading in that document, or the id of the PRD or TRD requirement; an empty string when the source has none.

Need.description: One thing the PRD needs of the architecture, and the architect's judgment of it.

id.description: N1, N2 and so on, unique in the file.

need.description: What the PRD needs, in one sentence.

prdRequirements.description: The PRD requirement headings the need comes from.

evidence.description: The approved statements judged, and for a disagreement the statements that disagree.

judgment.description: Why the state is what it is.

ArchitectureState.description: The solutions architect's answer to the request `Establish the state of the architecture for this PRD`, written before it does anything else.

FeatureEntry.description: One feature the PRD needs, as the architect recorded it in the matrix.

id.description: The matrix id of the feature row.

prdRequirements.description: The PRD requirement headings the feature serves.

elements.description: The matrix ids of the elements that realize it.

sharedCapabilities.description: The matrix ids of the supporting features it uses.

SharedUse.description: One behaviour one element obtains from a shared capability and does not implement itself.

element.description: The matrix id of the element that uses the capability.

capability.description: The matrix id of the supporting feature.

behaviour.description: The behaviour obtained, as the capability's `provides` entry states it.

FactEntry.description: One design fact with its one home.

id.description: The matrix id of the fact row.

statement.description: The fact, at architecture level, in the form its arc42 section requires.

home.description: The one arc42 document and heading that states the fact.

linkedFrom.description: The arc42 paths of the documents that link to the home and do not restate the fact.

CriterionAnswer.description: The architect's answer to one criterion of architecture-baseline/review-criteria.json whose level is architecture or technical-requirement.

satisfiedAt.description: For `satisfied`, each arc42 document and heading, or the TRD path with a requirement id as the heading, that satisfies it; empty for `not-applicable`.

reason.description: For `not-applicable`, why the criterion does not apply to this PRD; an empty string for `satisfied`.

SpecNote.description: One detail below architecture and technical-requirement level that is already known, kept for the spec authors.

element.description: The matrix id of the element the detail concerns.

detail.description: The route, field, key, parameter, name or schema detail.

source.description: Where the detail comes from: a path and heading, a URL, or `design` for something decided in this run.

Position.description: One of the positions on a matter.

id.description: A short name for the position, unique in the matter.

UnsettledMatter.description: A matter the architect could not settle, or the question the lead puts to the decider: the matter and the positions on it.

id.description: U1, U2 and so on, unique in the file.

matter.description: What has to be decided, in one or two sentences.

Choice.description: A decision the architect made between alternatives that each had a cost.

fact.description: The matrix id of the fact that states what was chosen.

alternatives.description: The alternatives that were not chosen.

CostEvidence.description: The unit math behind one cost constraint in the TRD.

resource.description: The matrix id of the billable element.

assumptions.description: The stated usage the estimate rests on.

unitMath.description: The arithmetic, with the fixed monthly floor kept apart from usage cost.

ReviewSignals.description: The facts about this run's design that the reviewer groups of architecture-baseline/review-criteria.json name in `appliesWhen.result`. A script selects reviewers from them; an empty list selects none.

failureBehaviours.description: The matrix ids of the facts this run decided that state retry, dead-letter, idempotent or recovery behaviour.

newRuntimeResources.description: The matrix ids of elements this run added that run in AWS.

newBillableResources.description: The matrix ids of elements this run added that AWS bills for and the approved design did not already hold.

changedBillableLimits.description: The TRD requirement ids whose limit or volume on an existing billable element this run changed.

newPatterns.description: The matrix ids of each new service, new shared capability, and element of a resource type the matrix had not held.

ArchitectureResult.description: The solutions architect's result for one Epic. The script reads `conclusion`, checks every criterion answer, and selects reviewers from `reviewSignals`; what is unapproved comes from the matrix, not from this file.

newElements.description: The matrix ids of the elements this run recorded.

facts.description: The design facts this run decided.

settledDisagreements.description: The matrix ids of the disagreements this run settled.

criteria.description: One answer for every criterion whose level is architecture or technical-requirement.

SpecialistRequest.description: What the solutions architect, or the lead when it asks for an opinion, asks of one design specialist or diagram author.

bounds.description: For a task, exactly what is to be decided and what is not; an empty string for a question.

concerns.description: The PRD sections and arc42 headings the request concerns, and nothing wider.

trustedCode.description: The matrix ids of elements whose code the matrix marks built or deployed. Code of any other element is a hint only.

answerPath.description: The absolute path the answer is written to.

NeededSpecialty.description: Another specialty the answer needs, for the architect to ask.

DesignFact.description: One decision a bounded task returns, for the architect to accept or change.

section.description: The arc42 section the fact belongs in: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8.

Diagram.description: One diagram for architecture-maintainer to place.

home.description: The arc42 document and heading the diagram belongs under.

viewType.description: The view type, from the documentation model's list of view types.

mermaid.description: The Mermaid source, without the code fence.

shows.description: The names of the elements the diagram shows.

SpecialistAnswer.description: A design specialist's or diagram author's answer to one request.

answer.description: The answer to the question in one sentence, or for a task what was decided in one sentence.

assumptions.description: What the answer rests on that the sources do not establish.

alternatives.description: The alternatives considered; empty unless the request asks for them.

decisions.description: For a task, the decisions as design facts; empty for a question.

diagrams.description: For a diagram task, the diagrams drawn; otherwise empty.

TrdChange.description: One change to the TRD. For `remove`, only `id` carries meaning and the other texts are empty.

id.description: The requirement id; for `add`, an empty string lets trd-author assign the next id.

statement.description: What must be true, with its checkable value.

appliesTo.description: The matrix id of the element.

TrdRequest.description: What the solutions architect asks of trd-author.

trdPath.description: The absolute path of the TRD file.

statePath.description: The absolute path of the architect's state file.

approvedHeadings.description: For `draft`, the approved arc42 headings and section 2 documents to draw standing obligations from; empty for `update`.

sharedCapabilities.description: For `draft`, each shared capability the design uses, to be written as one requirement of kind `reuse`; empty for `update`.

changes.description: For `update`, the changes to apply; empty for `draft`.

answerPath.description: The absolute path the answer is written to.

NoSource.description: An obligation the PRD implies for which neither the PRD nor the approved material gives a source.

prdRequirement.description: The PRD requirement heading that implies it.

why.description: What the architecture would have to state for the obligation to have a source.

TrdAnswer.description: trd-author's answer to one request. The TRD itself is the file at the request's `trdPath`.

requirementIds.description: For `draft`, every requirement id in the TRD; for `update`, the ids added, changed and removed.

Restatement.description: A place that states a fact a second time, to be replaced by a link to the fact's home.

fact.description: The id of the fact in this request, or the matrix id of an approved fact.

AppliedSettlement.description: A settled disagreement to apply to the documents.

disagreement.description: The matrix id of the disagreement row.

corrections.description: Each place whose statement lost and is replaced by a link to the one that stands.

WriteRequest.description: What the solutions architect asks architecture-maintainer to write into arc42.

resultPath.description: The absolute path the write result is written to.

entry.description: The id of the fact, or a description of the restatement, settlement or diagram.

WriteResult.description: architecture-maintainer's result for one write request.

linksAdded.description: Each place a link to a home heading was added.

belowArchitectureLevel.description: Entries not written because they are below architecture level, for the architect to move to the TRD or to notesForSpecs.

notApplied.description: Entries that could not be applied for any other reason.

ScopeFinding.description: One defect in one unapproved item, measured against one criterion at the item's own level.

id.description: F1, F2 and so on, unique in the review.

criterion.description: The id of the criterion the item does not meet.

item.description: The item of the review scope: a matrix row id, a document path and heading joined by `#`, or a TRD requirement id.

observation.description: What the item says or lacks, stated as a fact a reader can check.

correction.description: The bounded change that removes the defect.

doneWhen.description: The condition that shows the correction is made.

DependsOnApproved.description: An unapproved item that cannot be correct unless an approved statement is wrong.

AlternativeRequest.description: A request for a competing design of one item.

option.description: The option that was not considered.

why.description: Why it could plainly be better.

ScopeReview.description: One reviewer's result for the unapproved items its criteria apply to. Every item of its scope is in `passed` or has a finding, a `dependsOnApproved` report or an alternative request.

passed.description: The items that meet every criterion that applies to them.

RoutedItem.description: The lead's decision for one finding, alternative request or unsettled matter.

item.description: The finding id, the item of the alternative request, or the id of the unsettled matter.

raisedBy.description: The reviewer that raised it, or `aws-solutions-architect` for an unsettled matter.

steps.description: The ids of the journal steps the lead added for it; empty for `reject`.

LeadRouting.description: architecture-team-lead's output: one decision for each item it was started for.

requirements.description: The business requirements or section 2 constraints in conflict.

matter.description: The id of the matter in the question file.

stands.description: The id of the position that stands; an empty string only when an owner concern is raised.

reason.description: Why that position stands, from the evidence the two sides gave.

losingPositionChanges.description: What the losing position must change.

BuiltDifference.description: One difference, at architecture level, between code a Story built and the approved architecture.

element.description: The matrix id of the element.

code.description: Where the code shows it: repository, revision and file:line.

architecture.description: The approved arc42 heading it differs from.

difference.description: What the code does and what the architecture says, in one or two sentences.

document.description: The path, relative to the architecture root, of the built-difference document written for it.

BuiltComparison.description: built-architecture-comparer's result for one Story. An empty differences list means the code the Story built matches the approved architecture.
